title: Broccoli and Stilton Soup
subtitle: Creamy blended broccoli with Stilton stirred through
excerpt: Broccoli sweated in butter and blended smooth with hot vegetable stock, then finished with crumbled Stilton until it melts into the soup. A British restaurant classic that takes under 30 minutes.

recipe.sourceNotes: Broccoli and Stilton soup became a fixture of British pub and restaurant menus in the 1980s and 1990s as Stilton became more widely available and broccoli moved from a niche vegetable into mainstream UK cooking. Stilton is a PDO cheese made in Derbyshire, Leicestershire, and Nottinghamshire. The key technique is not to overcook the broccoli before blending: overcooked broccoli turns grey-green and loses its bright colour. Cook just until tender, then blend immediately.

recipeTools.notes: Or a stand blender for a smoother result.

content.text: Cook the broccoli briefly so the colour stays vivid green. Blend while still hot for the smoothest result. Add the Stilton off the heat: boiling the cheese will split it and make the soup grainy. If you want a very smooth result, pass through a fine sieve after blending.

items.preparation: cut into florets, stalk peeled and roughly chopped

content.text: Melt the butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion and a pinch of salt. Cook for 8 minutes until soft and translucent but not coloured. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the broccoli florets and stalk. Pour in the hot stock. Bring to a simmer and cook for 8 to 10 minutes until the broccoli is just tender but still bright green. Do not overcook.
Blend until very smooth with a stick blender or stand blender. Return to the pan if using a stand blender. Remove from the heat.
Stir in most of the Stilton until melted. Add the cream if using. Season with salt and pepper. Ladle into warm bowls and crumble the remaining Stilton over each serving.
